title: Dynamic HTML sink via document.write() — review required
description: A call to document.write() parses a string as HTML at runtime. If any part of the string is attacker-influenced this is cross-site scripting; even static uses block parsing and are banned by strict Content-Security-Policy. This lexical rule cannot prove taint — treat every hit as review-required.
remediation: Stop building HTML from strings: create elements with document.createElement and set text with textContent, or render through a framework that escapes by default. If HTML strings are unavoidable, sanitize with an allowlist-based sanitizer and a strict CSP.
limitation: Lexical, line-based, no dataflow: matches every document.write( call including static safe strings. document.writeln is out of scope for this rule.
